name: Times club monthly special crossword No 20,219

solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Discarded bits of gold line considered magical reflected American vanities

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the other way round, so the line's name is read backwards

blocks.note: a ley line is supposedly a track of mystical energy across the landscape
in the US a lowboy is a low dressing table, a vanity

explanation.surface: Someone throws out trinkets, gold thread and mirrored American dressing tables they once thought enchanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discarded' marks the definition as an obsolete word: yellowboys was old slang for gold coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellowboy is old slang, now out of use, for a gold sovereign or guinea, so pieces of gold money.

clue.text: Birchbark-oiled leather tent of Siberia with right side cut off almost-lowest part?

indicators.note: removing the right-hand side of the word leaves only its left half
almost signals that the word for the lowest part appears shortened, not whole

blocks.note: a yurt is the felt tent of Central Asian and Siberian nomads
the foot is the lowest part, and FT is its standard short form

explanation.surface: A description of how a Siberian tent is trimmed so its base is nearly gone, under a leathery heading.
explanation.walkthrough: The right side is the right-hand half of the word, and 'almost' asks for the abbreviation rather than the whole word for the lowest part.
explanation.definitionFit: Yuft is Russia leather, tanned hide dressed with birch-bark oil that gives it its distinctive smell.

clue.text: Release Australian plant-eater south of grassland

indicators.note: in a down entry, being south of something means sitting below it, so this piece comes second

blocks.note: a lea is a meadow or grassy field
vego is Australian slang for a vegetarian

explanation.surface: Instructions for freeing an Australian herbivore into pasture.
explanation.walkthrough: Plant-eater suggests a kangaroo or koala, but it is a person: Australians call a vegetarian a vego.
explanation.definitionFit: To let go of something is to stop holding it, which is to release it.

clue.text: “Overarching” philanthropist hot on ostrich cages

definitions.note: the clue gives an adjective; the answer is the noun for the condition

indicators.note: a cage holds something inside it, so the letters sit within the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across these words, from the end of the first into the start of the last

explanation.surface: A rich donor is keen on ostriches and keeps them enclosed.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around 'Overarching' warn that it is to be taken literally: the body arching over backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Opisthotonos is a spasm in which the back arches rigidly backwards, seen in tetanus, so the body is literally over-arched.

clue.text: Minor software problem that produces shrill reports?

blocks.note: first meaning: a little bug, with the diminutive ending -let
second meaning: a small bugle, which sounds piercing calls

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the first sense is invented: a small bug. Reports here are sounds, not error logs.
explanation.definitionFit: A buglet is a small bugle, a brass horn whose calls are high and piercing; the computing sense is a joke.

clue.text: One has permission to set about guenon monkey raised for forest-dwellers

indicators.note: setting something about another means placing it all round it
in a down entry, raising letters turns them so they read from the bottom up

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
if you may do something, you have permission
the mona is a West African guenon monkey

explanation.surface: Someone licensed to handle a guenon monkey brings it up to live in the forest.
explanation.walkthrough: A guenon is a kind of African monkey; the mona is one species. The whole assembly is read upwards, as this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yanomami are an indigenous people living in the Amazon rainforest of Venezuela and Brazil.

clue.text: Must for fermenting?

indicators.note: fermenting liquid bubbles and churns, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A winemaker's note about grape juice destined for fermentation.
explanation.walkthrough: The one word serves twice, as definition and as the letters to rearrange; the question mark flags the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Stum is unfermented or partly fermented grape juice, which is exactly what winemakers call must.

clue.text: Bring up half-forgotten Hawaiian dress scandal a few days before a feast

definitions.text: a few days before a feast

indicators.note: forgetting half of a word drops one half and keeps the other
in a down entry, bringing letters up means they read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a muumuu is a loose Hawaiian dress
dirt is scandalous gossip

explanation.surface: Someone raises an old scandal about a Hawaiian dress in the days before a big celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: The dress's name is a doubled syllable, so half of it is simply one repeat.
explanation.definitionFit: A triduum is a three-day period of prayer, often observed in preparation for a church festival.

clue.text: Recall Noah’s son, mostly groomed within religious schools

indicators.note: calling something back brings it the other way, so the name is read backwards
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter goes
within places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: Shem was one of Noah's three sons in Genesis
to be groomed is to be dressed and tidied

explanation.surface: Remembering how one of Noah's sons was smartly turned out at religious school.
explanation.walkthrough: Recall here is to call back, not to remember; it turns the son's name round.
explanation.definitionFit: Medresseh is a variant spelling of madrasa, an Islamic college or school of religious learning.

clue.text: Ruddy six-footer as Walloon’s rival?

blocks.note: both are mild euphemistic swear words, as in 'flaming nuisance'
an insect has six feet, and the ant is the crossword's usual one

explanation.surface: A red-faced very tall man is cast as the opponent of a Belgian.
explanation.walkthrough: Six-footer suggests a tall person, but it means anything with six legs. Walloons are French-speaking Belgians; their rivals are Flemish.
explanation.definitionFit: A flamingant is a Flemish nationalist in Belgium, politically opposed to the French-speaking Walloon community.

clue.text: Prisoner releases a one-pound rodent

indicators.note: releasing lets things go, so these letters leave the word

blocks.note: a jailbird is someone in prison
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: A convict lets go of a small animal weighing a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: JAILBIRD loses A, I and LB, leaving J and IRD.
explanation.definitionFit: A jird is a gerbil of North Africa and Asia, a small burrowing desert mammal of the mouse family.

clue.text: Once reproachful former right-winger gathering for support?

indicators.note: gathering something in takes it inside, so the pieces sit within the politician

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner, so ex means former
being pro something is being for it
a bra is a supporting undergarment
Tory is the everyday name for a UK Conservative

explanation.surface: An ex-Conservative who once scolded others now rounds up backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Former right-winger' looks like one unit, but its two halves sit either side of the support pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Exprobratory is an archaic word meaning upbraiding or censuring, hence once used to mean reproachful.

clue.text: Intensity of warmth, both reduced by flapping true spotted cloth

indicators.note: both of the first two words lose something, each being cut short by a letter
something flapping is thrown about, so its letters are tossed into a new order

blocks.note: heat is intensity, as in the heat of battle
thermic means relating to heat
x is the multiplication sign, read as 'by' in dimensions like 3 x 4
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fabric description: some flapping speckled cloth loses its warmth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intensity of warmth' reads as one phrase but splits in two, intensity and of warmth, and both words lose their last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Heather mixture is a woollen cloth woven with flecks of several colours, resembling heather, so speckled fabric.

clue.text: Poisonous smoke with auto fouled by internal combustion

indicators.note: something fouled is messed up, so the letters of the car are jumbled

blocks.note: a cig is a cigarette, a smoke
taken as written
x is the multiplication sign, read as 'by'
IC is the abbreviation for internal combustion

explanation.surface: Toxic fumes from a car whose engine has been fouled up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all exhaust fumes, but 'by' is the times sign and 'internal combustion' is just two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ciguatoxic describes fish carrying ciguatoxin, which causes ciguatera food poisoning in people who eat them.

clue.text: I repair junk: I live in Philippine mountains

definitions.note: the setter's 'I' does double duty: read with it, the answer speaks as 'I live in the mountains'; the answer itself is a noun for the person

blocks.note: taken as written
to repair to a place is to go there
rot is nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: A mountain dweller in the Philippines explains that they fix up scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: Repair suggests mending, but here it is the old sense of going somewhere. The definition speaks in the first person, as the answer would.
explanation.definitionFit: An Igorot is a member of the peoples of the Cordillera highlands of Luzon, so someone living in those mountains.

clue.text: Proper lives led by instant messaging in the first place

indicators.note: something led by another follows behind it, so the messaging piece goes first

blocks.note: IM is the usual abbreviation for instant messaging
prim means formally proper
to live is to be, so lives is is

explanation.surface: A prim person's life is now governed by texting before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprimis is Latin used in English to mean firstly, introducing the first item in a list.

clue.text: Object for lawyers is to protect witch and plug cracks in one’s case?

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding and shielding it

blocks.note: res is the Latin legal term for a thing, the object of a right
a hag is an ugly old witch
a plug is a bit of advertising, an ad

explanation.surface: Legal talk about protecting a witch and patching holes in an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's case' looks like a lawsuit, but it is the body's case, the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhagades are fissures or cracks in the skin, especially round the mouth, and skin is the body's covering.

clue.text: Reluctant to wear headless dummy’s strip

indicators.note: without a head the word loses its first letter
something worn is held around, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: loth means unwilling
a dummy is a stupid person, a dunce

explanation.surface: A mannequin missing its head does not want to be dressed in a team strip.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip looks like sports kit, a noun, but it is the verb, to undress.
explanation.definitionFit: To unclothe someone is to remove their clothes, which is what it means to strip them.

clue.text: Stick with bent head master in jug?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree
a crock is an earthenware pot or jar

explanation.surface: A walking stick with a hooked handle, with a schoolmaster stuck in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Jug invites the slang sense of prison, but it is an earthenware vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A cromack, also crummock, is a Scottish shepherd's staff with a crooked or curved handle.

clue.text: Aberdeen’s distant: return its grant to stop minor injury

indicators.note: returning goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards
stopping something plugs it, so this piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: 'its' points back to Aberdeen: gie is the Scots form of give, to grant
ABH is actual bodily harm, a lesser assault charge than GBH

explanation.surface: A Scottish city sits far off while someone reverses a grant meant to halt an injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aberdeen's' marks a Scots word, and 'its' asks for the Scots word for grant too. ABH, actual bodily harm, is a British criminal charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Abeigh is a Scots adverb meaning aloof or at a distance, so Aberdeen's word for far off.

clue.text: US president more than half crazy, exhibiting array of bloomers

indicators.note: keeping more than half of a word means the end is cut off but most survives

blocks.note: Ike was the nickname of President Eisenhower
going bananas is going crazy

explanation.surface: A slightly unhinged American president puts on a show of underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloomers suggests old-fashioned knickers, but here they are flowers. BANANAS keeps four of its seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ikebana is the Japanese art of flower arranging, and flowers are things that bloom.

clue.text: Crippled by indecision, regularly ignored and upset: chill out, brah!

indicators.note: ignoring at regular intervals skips every other letter
in a down entry, upset turns letters over so they read upwards

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and following letters

explanation.surface: A surfer tells an anxious friend who cannot make up their mind to relax.
explanation.walkthrough: Brah is surfer slang for brother. Odd letters kept, then read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Abulia is a loss of willpower and decisiveness, so someone abulic is unable to make decisions.

clue.text: Violent bishop accepted by God passed easily in America, having leather straps

indicators.note: being accepted by someone means being taken in, so these go inside the god

blocks.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder
rough means violent, as in rough play
B is the chess notation for bishop
in US usage to ace an exam is to pass it easily

explanation.surface: A rough bishop, received by God, sails through his American exams.
explanation.walkthrough: A thoroughbrace is the leather strap on which an old coach body hangs; the term is mainly American.
explanation.definitionFit: A thoroughbraced carriage hangs on long leather straps called thoroughbraces running front to back.

clue.text: Catfish killed when coming from the bottom

indicators.note: in a down entry, starting at the bottom means the letters read upwards

blocks.note: slew is the past tense of slay, to kill

explanation.surface: A bottom-feeding catfish that kills from the riverbed.
explanation.walkthrough: Catfish are bottom-feeders, so 'from the bottom' sounds like a hunting habit; in a down entry it is the reading direction.
explanation.definitionFit: The wels is a very large European freshwater catfish, also called the sheatfish.

clue.text: Christian soldier statues were buried here in China

definitions.text: soldier statues were buried here in China

blocks.note: first meaning: the written abbreviation, with X for Christ

blocks.clueFragment: soldier statues were buried here in China
blocks.note: second meaning: the Chinese city near the Terracotta Army

explanation.walkthrough: 'Christian soldier' reads as one phrase, after the hymn, but the clue splits after 'Christian'. The Chi-Rho tradition gives X for Christ.
explanation.definitionFit: Xian is a short written form of Christian, and Xi'an in Shaanxi is where the terracotta warriors were found.

clue.text: Tricky to read clue free of impurities amenable to solution

definitions.text: free of impurities amenable to solution

indicators.note: something tricky is awkward to handle, so the words that follow are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A solver complains about a hard clue that must be cleaned up before it can be solved.
explanation.walkthrough: Solution means a chemical one, not the answer to a puzzle; free is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To edulcorate is to wash a substance to remove soluble impurities, or more generally to sweeten or purify.

clue.text: Reminder that there’s potassium in long green fruit

indicators.note: saying something is there in another places it inside

blocks.note: a cue is a prompt to remember a line or action
K is the chemical symbol for potassium

explanation.surface: A dietary reminder that a long green fruit contains potassium.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like nutrition advice about bananas; the fruit here is a cucumber.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuke is informal, chiefly American, for a cucumber, botanically a fruit that is long and green.

clue.text: I deeply lament abuse about climate indicators

indicators.note: turning about faces the other way, so the word for abuse is read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
so is an intensifier, as in 'I so want that'
to cry is to lament
to slam someone is to criticise them harshly

explanation.surface: Someone grieves heavily over mistreatment of the climate.
explanation.definitionFit: Isocrymals are map lines joining places with the same lowest winter temperature, so they show climate patterns.
